title: Staining of Cells with GolgiTracker for Flow Cytometry Analysis
author: Enrico Bagnoli
materials: Isolation of intact Golgi using GolgiTag immunoprecipitation method
Preparation of samples for flow cytometry.
Perform statistical analysis using Prism software or equivalent.
Open the software and drag the samples to be analyzed in the main window

steps.title: Prepare GolgiTracker Stock
steps.instruction: Prepare a 500 µM stock of GolgiTracker in DMSO and dissolve thoroughly by vortexing.

steps.title: Prepare Cells
steps.instruction: Grow HEK293 cells stably expressing GolgiTag or ControlTag in 10cm 2 Petri dishes until near confluent.

substeps.instruction: Prepare two plates for each experimental condition: one for GolgiTracker staining and one control plate (not stained).

steps.title: Stain Cells with GolgiTracker
steps.instruction: Add GolgiTracker to the cells to a final concentration of 5 µM (1:100 dilution).

substeps.instruction: Add DMSO vehicle (1% v/v) to control cells.

steps.title: Incubate Cells
steps.instruction: Incubate the cells at 37 °C for 30 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Discard media and add fresh media before the final 30-minute incubation at 37 °C.

steps.title: Perform Golgi Immunoprecipitation
steps.instruction: Perform Golgi immunoprecipitation as described in dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6qpvrdjrogmk/v1.

substeps.instruction: At the end (Step 56 of the referenced protocol), add 500 µL KPBS to the beads instead of lysis buffer and gently resuspend by pipetting up and down.

steps.title: Prepare Flow Cytometer
steps.instruction: Prepare the cytometer for sample acquisition.

substeps.instruction: Turn on the machine following relative SOPs (perform starting procedure if first user of the day).
Check that the waste container is not full and the buffer container is not empty; refill or empty as needed.

steps.title: Prepare Samples for Flow Cytometry
steps.instruction: Dilute the final IPs for analysis.

substeps.instruction: Prepare and label appropriate FACS tubes (e.g., GolgiTAG +Tracker, GolgiTAG -Tracker, HA-Empty +Tracker, HA-Empty -Tracker).
Perform a 1:100 or 1:200 dilution: take 40 µL from the 500 µL KPBS/Beads mixture and resuspend in a FACS tube with 400 µL KPBS on ice.

steps.title: Configure Cytometer Parameters
steps.instruction: Set up the BD LSR Fortessa parameters and gates.

substeps.instruction: Set the FITC channel for tracker analysis.
Configure three windows: Forward scatter (FSC) vs Side scatter (SSC), Histogram of FITC channel, and FITC vs FSC.
If running for the first time, adjust voltages for FSC, SSC, and FITC. Optimized voltages for LSR Fortessa are: SSC: 231, FSC: 566, FITC: 400.
Use a logarithmic scale for scatters.
Run samples with the highest and lowest signals to ensure operation within the linear range of the cytometer.
Ensure all events are inside the window and not on the edges; note that beads are approximately 1 µm in diameter.

steps.title: Acquire Samples
steps.instruction: Run the samples once voltages are optimized.

substeps.instruction: Record at least 20k events per sample (50k is preferred).

steps.title: Clean and Save Data
steps.instruction: Clean the machine and save the data as FCS 3.0 files.

steps.title: Analyze Data using FlowJo
steps.instruction: Process the acquired data to quantify GolgiTracker positive beads.

substeps.instruction: Gate the beads from the SSC and FSC plot (use height instead of area or width for small samples like organelle IPs to exclude broken beads and debris).
Calculate the % of GolgiTracker+ beads from the FITC vs FSC plot or the FITC histogram.
Calculate mean FITC intensity, mean SSC, and FSC values for the gated beads.
Create tables and graphs of the relevant samples in the workspace.
Export tables in an excel compatible format and images in PNG or PowerPoint format.
